answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer: engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically, and if not fixed within 3 days, the laptop loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

answers.reasoning_note: Answered from KB-27 v1.2 (effective Feb 1, 2026) §4, which KB-07 §3.4 and KB-22 back up. The 2024 past answers in KB-32 (A-058, A-059) agree but are less authoritative, so they were not cited.

No retrieved passage mentions a bug bounty or rewards. Related: KB-16 §8 (v1.3) describes vulnerability disclosure: reports go to security@tidewelldata.example and are acknowledged within 3 business days. A reviewer could use this if a disclosure-only answer is acceptable.

No passage says whether the full pentest report is shared under NDA. Related: Trust Center (KB-01) lists only a "Penetration Test Summary Letter" as "On request"; KB-17 is that Brightline letter (May 29, 2026). Only the SOC 2 full report is stated as available under NDA (KB-04).

No passage says whether there is a 24/7 SOC or around-the-clock staffing. Related: KB-06 §7 covers automated detection rules, alerts sent to the Security team's queue, and escalation per the IR Plan. KB-10 §6.2 sets SEV1 triage within 30 minutes. Neither states coverage hours.

answers.answer: Under the current Information Security Policy (v3.2), the Head of Security owns the security program day to day. That role maintains security policies and standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the program, and a Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls. Our documents do not name the person in the role, and they do not give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer. KB-02 v3.2 gives the security leadership roles but no CISO title, no name, and no team headcount. Superseded KB-03 v2.4 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32 A-012) name the Director of Engineering as owner. That is outdated and was not used.
